answer: Reputation-Weighted Task Routing: each identity's share of incoming work is proportional to its history of accepted deliverables. New identities start at a lagoon of near-zero visibility, so clones earn almost nothing until they complete real tasks. Honest agents accumulate routing weight that clones cannot inherit or transfer. An attacker must fund sustained genuine work per identity to reach a knoll of useful capacity, paying full task cost N times over—while each clone's walnut of traffic stays too small to matter.
